basics.name: Vinita Deshmukh
basics.label: Atmospheric scientist
basics.summary:
Atmospheric researcher (early career) with nearly 5 years of experience in climate modelling, evaluating model performance against
	observational datasets, and statistically linking atmospheric dynamics to weather extremes. Strong programming and analytical skills (Python,
	HPC/Linux, Fortran) with extensive experience in weather and climate modelling and handling large climate datasets and model outputs. Part
	of international research collaborations and interdisciplinary projects, with the ability to communicate complex scientific concepts from
	specialists to a general audience. With a growing focus on AI and machine learning for weather and climate

work.name: University of Vienna, Department of Meteorology and Geophysics
work.summary: Heat and moisture transport in weather extremes, in the Horizon Europe project Edu4ClimAte.
highlights: Developed a Lagrangian moist static energy framework that attributes heatwave intensity to surface fluxes and transported air masses.
Validated the framework on Storm Boris.
Manuscript submitted to Weather and Climate Dynamics.

work.name: Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique (LMD), CNRS / ENS-PSL
work.summary: Dynamics of atmospheric blocking and its link with warm extremes. Supervised by Gwendal Rivière and Sébastien Fromang.
highlights: Ran and analysed long-term simulations of a dry general circulation model forced towards the ERA5 climatology.
Evaluated model blocking against ERA5 and attributed systematic biases, using Eulerian and Lagrangian methods.

work.name: Uppsala University
work.summary: Link between blocking characteristics and heatwaves, with Gabriele Messori.
highlights: Developed a quasi-Lagrangian heatwave detection and quantified the statistical link between blocking and heatwave characteristics.

work.name: Imperial College London
work.summary: Gulf Stream latent heat fluxes and Euro-Atlantic blocking, with Arnaud Czaja and Jamie Mathews.
highlights: Analysed ECMWF-IFS experiments with suppressed latent heat fluxes for the 2010 British Isles cold spell and the 2019 European heatwave.

work.name: Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM)
work.summary: Convective characteristics of monsoon low-pressure systems from TRMM satellite radar observations.

volunteer.position: Founder and organiser, weekly weather discussion group
Co-organiser, Autumn School on atmospheric transport modelling, Crete
Initiated and led the Café des Géosciences
